city_center.notes: 'The Magic City' -- an iron-and-steel town in the Appalachian foothills. Publix and Winn-Dixie both serve the metro; Piggly Wiggly has local roots. Sloss Furnaces produced pig iron from 1882 to 1971 and is now a preserved landmark. sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sloss_Furnaces; encyclopediaofalabama.org.

cultural_notes: Birmingham is 'The Magic City,' founded on iron and steel; Sloss Furnaces operated as a pig-iron blast furnace from 1882 to 1971 and is now one of the first industrial sites in the US preserved for public use (source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sloss_Furnaces; encyclopediaofalabama.org; birminghamal.gov)
The region's iron heritage comes from an unusual local abundance of the three minerals needed to make iron -- ore, coal, and limestone -- all near Birmingham (source: hmdb.org Ironmaking marker)

Chilton County, just south of Birmingham, is Alabama's famous peach country; Alabama peaches run May through September and sweet potatoes are harvested mid-July through November (source: aces.edu Fruit Culture in Alabama; alabamafarmtoece.org AL produce seasons)

Birmingham holds deep significance in the American civil-rights movement; reference the city's history respectfully and never trivialize it (source: general historical knowledge -- honor gravity, no trivializing)
